name: Ben Sasse
role: Former U.S. senator from Nebraska (2015–2023) and University of Florida president (2023–2024); announced terminal stage-four pancreatic cancer in December 2025
summary: Sasse is a conservative Republican who campaigned for repeal of the Affordable Care Act, opposes abortion, backs free trade and strong alliances, and favours limited, decentralized government and Congress reclaiming lawmaking power from agencies. He was a frequent critic of Donald Trump and voted to convict him in 2021. His speeches stress civic pluralism, local institutions and the dignity of persons over partisan power.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Called himself the national anti-ObamaCare candidate and promised to repeal it; said uninsurance from job change can be fixed through portable private insurance 'without the federal government'.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Official site: 'Government doesn't grow the economy; the private sector does.' 2014 platform: nothing matches the private sector's creativity and responsiveness.

property-fundamental.rationale: 2014 platform lists 'protecting property' among government's proper tasks; no statement on how hard it should be to override.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Campaign platform: products and services do not become more efficient by being more heavily regulated; backed rolling back the regulatory state and voted for the 2018 bank-regulation relief bill.

cut-welfare.rationale: 2014 platform opposed 'spawning dependency' and called for repealing unaffordable new entitlements while reforming existing ones; also voted for a 2020 COVID relief package that included SNAP money.

surveillance-ok.rationale: 2014 debate: government must have technology to keep up with bad actors but must guard against unreasonable search and seizure.

strong-leader.rationale: Farewell address rejects 'I alone can fix it' and a 'Caesarist solution'; says centralized power is the false prophets' answer and the Constitution's separation of powers must be kept.

state-harmful.rationale: Official site and platform call protection of citizens the government's first duty and describe a limited government that protects historic freedoms.

limit-guns.rationale: 2014 platform: Second Amendment right 'is inviolable' and stricter laws won't deter criminals; in 2022 he opposed the Senate gun bill over due-process and constitutional-rights concerns.

empower-police-military.rationale: Platform calls for spending to keep 'the greatest fighting force' and he backed funding to prosecute gun crimes; no position found on police authority.

decide-locally.rationale: Official site: most good policy is made at state and local level; farewell praises federalism over administrative centralization; Dobbs statement prefers debate in the 50 states.

traditional-family.rationale: Official site: the family is the most basic unit of civilization; 2014 platform: marriage and traditional families are critical to a republic.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: 2014 platform: marriage as one man and one woman 'should be respected and strengthened, not redefined'; called Obergefell a disappointment and said voters should decide in the states; abstained on the Respect for Marriage Act; in 2022 said Obergefell is the law of the land.

abortion-legal.rationale: 2014: life begins at conception; sponsored the Born-Alive Act; hailed Dobbs as righting a constitutional wrong; opposed the Women's Health Protection Act.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: 2014 platform: American sovereignty undergirds international commitments and multilateralism is a pragmatic tool, not an end in itself.

free-trade.rationale: 'Trade is indisputably good for America... good for consumers on both sides'; 'More trade is always a win-win'; voted for USMCA.

nation-first.rationale: Says leadership and alliances serve US interests but also that global disengagement hurts America and the world.

open-borders.rationale: 2014 platform: Americans are not safe unless we know who enters and leaves; voted against ending the 2019 border emergency.

limit-growth.rationale: Backs growth by rolling back regulation and expanding energy production; says climate answer is innovation, not alarmism.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Called the Green New Deal 'too big, too expensive, and out of touch with reality'; says innovation, not alarmism, is the answer.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Says innovation is the way through challenges, but a 2026 summary has him doubting that abundance alone solves human problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: 2014 debate: supports renewables, ethanol, wind and 'clean nuclear power'.

experts-over-public.rationale: Criticizes experts in Washington who don't stand for election imposing rules; says laws should be written by elected officials.

central-planning.rationale: Decried the 'Solyndra strategy'; platform says government should not orchestrate life and private sector is more efficient.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: 'Tariffs always hurt us'; 'nobody ever wins a trade war'; called Trump's steel and aluminum tariffs a terrible idea.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Opposed 'an administration that tries to pick winners and losers'; voted to kill reauthorization of the Export-Import Bank.

direct-votes.rationale: Maiden speech approves having a representative rather than direct democracy so representatives can mitigate polarization.

political-violence-never.rationale: After Dobbs: 'There is no room for political violence in America – none. Mob violence is un-American, period.'

separate-church-state.rationale: Praised Kennedy v. Bremerton: government may not suppress a school employee's personal prayer; no statement on strict separation as such.

military-superiority.rationale: Platform: maintain 'the greatest fighting force the world has ever seen'; supports peace through strength.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Farewell: 'You can come from anywhere in the world and be one with us'; condemns anti-pluralists who are 'against minorities... against diversity'.

equal-outcomes.rationale: 2014 platform: government should not focus on 'equalizing outcomes'.

total-state.rationale: 2014 platform: churches and civil associations protect against 'all-encompassing statism'; government should tread lightly and not orchestrate life.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: 2018: the idea that there is no truth is 'corrosive to a democracy'; cited Moynihan that no one is entitled to their own facts.

universal-morality.rationale: 2014 platform: America rests on universal values grounded in human dignity; farewell cites dignity from the creator.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Attacked deficit-financed spending bills (ARPA, 2022 omnibus, Inflation Reduction Act) but voted for the Dec 2020 $900 billion COVID relief law.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Reformed Christian elder who ties dignity and politics to faith and the soul; the farewell speech speaks of souls and making peace with God.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Supports the Keystone XL pipeline and more North American oil and gas, opposed the 'war on coal'; wants shale-driven energy independence.

national-mission.rationale: 2014 platform commits to promoting religious freedom, human rights and democracy but with skepticism of military entanglements.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Says 'politicians have worked hard to earn that hate', introduced an ethics package, and campaigned against 'influence peddlers' in Washington.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Farewell speaks of the 'universal dignity' every person has from the creator; 2014 platform grounds America in universal values of human dignity.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Says laws must be written by 'people who can be hired and fired on Election Day' and that unelected agencies conflict with self-government.

separated-powers.rationale: Maiden speech, Kavanaugh opening statement and farewell all defend Madisonian separation of powers and Congress's Article I role.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Welcomed the Senate approving Finland and Sweden joining NATO; said retreating from alliances would embolden China and that strong alliances deter Putin and Xi.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Cosponsored the EACH Act (religious exemption from the insurance mandate) and defended health providers' conscience rights.

collective-defense.rationale: Praised NATO as the 'greatest strategic alliance in world history'; said 'We will defend our ally Taiwan'.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Farewell calls Putin 'an evil man who thinks he can seize land that is not his' in Ukraine.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Farewell rejects a 'Caesarist' answer and defends the limited Constitution; said Trump pardons were 'rotten to the core' and voted to convict over the oath of office.

leader-cult.rationale: Responding to the state GOP: 'Politics isn't about the weird worship of one dude'; farewell rejects strongman politics.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Farewell calls the limited Constitution and separated powers essential and rejects moving past them; defended the filibuster to protect minority rights and dissent.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Farewell praises the Constitution as limiting government to protect free exercise of religion, speech, assembly and a free economy; platform calls the Second Amendment inviolable.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Urges civic re-engagement and representative government; but says Washington is a temporary stay before returning to community.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: A 2014 campaign report says he endorsed some form of Social Security privatization; not found in his own words.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Said Congress, not the President, must approve student-loan relief; called Trump's 2020 stimulus executive order 'unconstitutional slop'.

national-law-over-international.rationale: 2014 platform: American sovereignty undergirds international legal commitments; also signed a letter opposing Palestinian ICC membership.

religion-illusion.rationale: Reformed Christian elder; farewell treats the soul and one's relation to God as real matters the state must not obstruct.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Says the main divide is pluralists versus zealots rather than red versus blue, but rejects 'mushy middle' and says policy debates matter.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Defends NATO membership as good for America and criticizes colleagues who rejected it.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Repeatedly opposed executive rule by decree: OSHA mandate ('unconstitutional slop'), Biden student-loan scheme, EPA rulemaking; says laws must come from people elected by voters.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: 2014 platform calls churches and charities the 'lifeblood of society'; says government should not create communities. No direct comparison with aid programs.

term-limits.rationale: Pledged a 12-year limit in 2014, cosponsored a constitutional amendment (two Senate terms, three House terms) and argued for term limits at a Judiciary subcommittee hearing.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Maiden speech: reducing everything to good versus evil is bad history; farewell: 'politics won't save us'.

second-chamber.rationale: Maiden speech: even in a thought experiment, many great things would be lost without the Senate; explains the Senate's purpose beside the House.

person-over-state.rationale: Farewell: the Constitution rejects absolute power because souls cannot be compelled by force; the state may not stand in the way of persons' conscience.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Farewell says people are 'in-souled' and government should respect them as souls; 'politics won't save us'.

student-debt-relief.rationale: 'Flatly unjust to transfer poorer Americans' earnings to fund richer folks' graduate degrees'; opposed Biden's relief plan.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Farewell describes a 'shared anthropology' of people with dignity from their creator; does not address redesign.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Voted against the FIRST STEP Act, which reduced some mandatory minimums for repeat drug offenders; a vote only, reasons not found.

indirect-election.rationale: Wikipedia reports he proposed repealing the Seventeenth Amendment so state legislatures would choose senators; primary source not found.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: On Social Security: 'the poorest and sickest among us' should be taken care of first and he accepted some means testing.

no-business-privileges.rationale: 2014 platform: regulations should not disadvantage everyday Americans 'at the expense of the well-connected' and tax code should drop special-interest loopholes.

multipolar-world.rationale: 2018: 'U.S. global leadership is indispensable'; 'When the United States doesn't lead, chaos inevitably follows.'

notes: Full texts of his books (The Vanishing American Adult, Them) were not reachable, so no answers rest on them. Several 2014 positions come from his campaign platform as reproduced by OnTheIssues. Votes were taken from OnTheIssues' vote pages, not congress.gov. Dec 2020 COVID relief yes vote versus later opposition to deficit spending is treated as mixed. Verified living as of 2026 via Wikipedia (diagnosis announced 23 Dec 2025).
